items.title: AI as the ultimate leverage
items.contentHtml:
There seem to be 2 main advantages for AI use (for me rn): knowing what you want and judgement. They are kind of related, but while the first one is about human leverage against other humans, the second comes from advantage against AI and all humans. 
When thinking about it, what the ultimate usage and state of AI would be, I remembered of the Hayek paper "The Use of Knowldege in Society". Specifically, the point about specific knowledge. There are things, that by nature, are knowledge specific and cannot be aggregated to make decisions. Thinking in this context, my parallel was that in the end, humans are going to have different inputs because they have different lives. Better life. Better AI usage

items.title: How to be a better person
items.contentHtml:
Want to get healthier. Eat protein and vegetablesWant to get stronger. Go to the gymWant to get more intelligent. Read booksThere are a lot of mainstream and common knowledge shit about being a "better" person. Yes, stronger, healthier and more intelligent are better. However, religion, meditation, journaling and all those other things are not treated in the same way as the three examples in the top. They are all, without a doubt, mechanisms and protocols humans (or God) create that should have an effect to become a better person.

What do they have in common?

Fuel: Why? What is yout fucking motivation?Specification? What are you doing that it will make you a better person? What exactly types of outputs are you searchingRepetition? Going to masses? what is the repetitive behavior you are having that will make you a better person?Field? What is the place, both physical and non-physical that you implement this.Detection? How am I going to percieve that I am getting closer or not to the target?I've always felt that I hand a really easy job in incorporating behaviors and attitudes I read. I can see how a lot of buffet/munger ideas I read when I was younger, or how Dostoevsky saying "never lie to yourself" have changed my approach and inner working. I was/am always fast in incorporating feedback. This yielded me the question: how can I implement this in a better way. What type of mechanisms can I create in my life to do so. What can my moral gym be?

Mechanism proposition

0. Motivation (I want to be a better person).1. Define a specification (what is the type of behavior/reaction I am trying to acquire). Keep with it for 90 days.2. Go to the Church (Duke Chapel is what I mean here)3. Enter in your app. Go to the "xx/xx/20xx" section. Do the 10 times breath exercise Rod showed to get "in the present". Go over your past day, looking at how many times you did not achieved the virtue. And how many you did. Read the short-term piece about someone implementing the virtue. It can be Jesus, Buddha, Munger or anyone else you deeply respect. Imagine/mentalize what could be the different behavior in your bad situations. Pray 1/5 of the Holy Rosary. 10 times breath exercise. Leave.4. During the day, write every time you weren't complacent with the virtue. Let's see.

items.title: Agency 1
items.contentHtml:
This is named Agency 1 because I’m sure there will be many more about it. This is a topic that rlly catches my attention. Firstly, because it’s hard for me to define it. Secondly, because it looks rlly powerful. Thirdly, because I  can see it in my life.
My thought to write here is how shyness is a bottleneck to agency. In the same way laziness, procrastination and don’t believing in yourself ade, shyness is also one. And this is relevant because is the one I have to deal the most. It’s improving, but in the same way laziness don’t allow you to be intellectually agentic, shyness won’t allow to be socially agrntic. And that matters as fuck (rod example of being accepted into Duke).
This resembles one conclusion I know it has been a while: the most important thing I need to do is to reach the same level I have with consciousness, neuroticism and iq for people skills or whatever you wanna call it.

items.title: What I learned at Verde
items.contentHtml:
This is the third time I am writing this. The other two went wrong. Fuck the BS, let's get into what matters, learnings in hf stuff, AI and life.

Hedge Fund Stuff

1. Excel without mouse - makes life easier and more colorful. No friction. Just direct work
2. How markets rlly work - this is hard to define exactly, but before Verde, Faria Lima/Wall Street was a idealist company. "sell-side", "earnings preview", "expectations" were all kind of idealist terms that reflect much more stronger views than actually are. I talked with sell-side. I did my earnings preview. They fucking bought the stock. They are just people, smart (sometimes) people doing their job, hoping to get promoted, get rich and spend with their families (or at Vila). Sell-side reports are not sacred art works which represent the maximum level of enterprise intelligence society has achieved. They are just some junior analyst writing numbers that the senior analyst said while the partner was thinking if this was going to hurt company reputation. Every time you think they are some kind of fucking genius, remember that story about the education company who released 4 semesters instead of 3 in their earnings. They released saying it was a error. The stock grew by two-figures in the next day (just to make it clear THEY SAID IT WAS A FUCKING ERROR). Not just that, in the next year, the analysts FUCKING forgot that the number in the model in the previous year was wrong and, using that as parameters, grew their numbers by roughly 33% of what it should be. Like, what'd fuck.
3. How to think about stocks - there are three components to return: earnings increase, multiple re-rating, dividends. It all boils down to those three. That's what matter.
4. DDM > DCF - kind of contrarian here, but it's a rlly interesting approach. in the end is the money that you are receiving through dividends that matters. They should be close to each other (mainly DDM to FCFE) but they are not. Interesting take
5. Modelling stuff - not just excel. But like. How to properly do a fuckin 3sm. 
6. Building a portfolio - x-axis assimetry. y-axis conviction. markovitz in action. Simple, visual, but insightful about what matters. 
7. Hypothesis - How a thesis should look like. Testable, measurable, specific. Exactly like a popper scientific hypothesis (wooow). That is cool. Making a scientific approach is exactly the type of intelectual shit I like about markets. Not BS, but a real philosophy to make work better.

AI

8. Explicit x Implicit - That is the one I want to dive and learn the most. The problem with AI use is that we don't a know a bunch of shit we know. That's what they call "judgement" or "taste". These are the things we can make and we know. But we cannot teach. Because it is implicit. I have to read more and learn here, but for me this seems to be part of the bottleneck of becoming an AI powered human being. (the other part is knowing what you want. and that's even harder, but more later)
9. When you know what you want, you're set - my boss only wanted a dashboard where he could see the information that mattered, and some skill that did the modelling for him. simple. sweet. my only job was to ask claude to make it, and ask again when said it didn't. like, you just need to ask and don't be a retarded. Just agency (or whatever that word is supposed to mean)
10. It's about the mindset - what can I simplify in my life. Do i know what I want? do I know what is explicit x implicit? Done. Totally done. In the same way founders say that you became "passion by the problem" and all that SEO bs, if you just try to solve problems in your own life, u should be fine

Life

All of the previous ones were also a huge part thankfully to Antonio. But I think those below are even more. I think overall he has a similar intelectual curiosity as I do. So a bunch of his approach and thinking are exactly the things I found the most interesting.
11. The process - this one could be up in hf stuff, but is more than that. Is all about the process. Trust the process. This is our process. every. fucking. time.That's what I heard at my time there. The process to build something great, that works. Create it, work on it and trust it. That's for hf. for gym. for everything. 
12. What is the best framework - I've lost many thinking hours wondering about the "framework", or the "MECE structure" I should use to think about stuff. fuck it. It is all frameworks. it's the map. it's, by definition, wrong and incomplete. Just think about the goal and use some initial mental model/framework that will help get there. "oh, but should I use this approach, or this other one that ortogonal? but this is incomplete, it lacks depth". shut the fuck up.
13. Divergence x Convergence - There are two phases to every exploration. Divergence. Convergence. Firstly, you don't know what you don't know. There is no path, no short-cut. Just complete exploration. After learning and having your info, comes convergence. framework creation. having the map.
14. Psychopaths win - arrived at 6am every fucking morning. earlier than the ones below. earlier than the ones above. Focus.
15. Sometimes you need to shine. Mostly, just don't do shit - The companies that I've studied they had one thing in common: they only needed to don't do shit. And I think the same applies to many of the interactions. No one is remembered for something good at a restaurant. or when waiting in line. you'll be remembered if you do some shit. sometimes need to take the risk and shine. others, just to don't do shit
16. No one. absolutely no one. gives a fuck about you - your boss has a family. a wife. a job. no one cares about you. just give what they fucking want.
17. Is all about people - Bahia vibes here. connection is what matters.

items.title: Removing Friction
items.contentHtml:
I wanna do X. I am in Y. What are the things that do not matter and that make this transition harder?

That is friction. 
  • Want to learn about x? Have to spend time going across tabs, twitter, spotify, etc. Friction.
  • Want to recruit for IB? Have to spend time keeping track of emails, answers, etc. Friction.
Removing friction is important because of two main factors. Firstly, it takes time. No one wants do spend time on shit that no one gives a fuck. Secondly, and I think the most important one: it reduces the enthusiasm and willingness to do what really matters. Living 2min from the gym? Amazing. No lazy excuses. Have to take 3 buses, 2 trains, and walk 3 miles. No fucking way. What are the "frictions" of my life? Can AI solve any of them?
  • Learning -> Solved
  • Recruiting and keeping track of all the BS -> In process
  • What else there is? Beyond removing shit that does not matter, how can it empower the ones that do?
